newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cardoso calls on Brazilians to back reform drive.
newsitem.headline: Cardoso calls on Brazilians to back reform drive.

text.p: President Fernando Henrique Cardoso on Monday urged Brazilians to pressure Congress to approve a host of constitutional reforms seen necessary to secure the gains achieved under his three-year-old Real Plan.
"It is a minority in Congress that blocks the changes," Cardoso told an audience of businessmen at the opening of an international conference on integration and development.
"The government needs the society's help. It needs society's pressure," Cardoso said.
He said many reforms had been approved in a short period of time, such as the new General Telecommunications Law, a bill opening the oil sector to private capital and a new corporate law.
But the country still faces the challenge of approving key constitutional amendments to reform its pension and civil service systems, he added.
"If we don't resolve the pension issue, the youth of today will not have social security in the future," Cardoso said.
Cardoso said a main achievement of the Real Plan, which has slashed inflation from nearly 3,000 percent three years ago to about eight percent today, was to create predictability.
"Brazil is tired of the zigzag, the suspense," he said.
Cardoso said he would not veer from his anti-inflation focus and attacked those who criticize his government for not addressing poverty, health care and other social issues.
"Don't talk to me about social issues. We will keep fighting for social developments, but taking measures independently from their popularity," he said.

Cardoso frequently points out that cutting inflation alone has been the quickest way to improve the quality of life for millions of Brazil's poor. He has noted that the poor are eating more meat and are buying appliances and other goods at record levels thanks to the plan's success.
The president also defended his government against critics who charge it has no vision for the future.
"How can they say we don't have a project? We have a project that will not be built by the state, but by society with the state's help," he said.
